issues.description: Timeout-based End-frame mechanism races with stream-completion and breaks the Start/End bookend invariant.
issues.detail: A 1.0s sleep task pushes LLMFullResponseEndFrame while process_frame also closes at end-of-stream. With shared _output_response_open and no lock, overlapping or in-flight invocations can interleave bookends, double-close, or drop the End. The stream has a deterministic end; emit Start before the loop, End after, and delete the timer.

issues.description: default_response_to_output_transformer raises JSONDecodeError on non-JSON lines, aborting the stream and leaving bookends unbalanced.
issues.detail: json.loads runs inside the per-line loop with no try/except. A heartbeat, comment, or malformed SSE line propagates out of process_frame, leaving _output_response_open=True and the End frame unsent. Either guard the parse and return None on failure, or document transformers as total and enforce at the boundary.

issues.description: bedrock-agentcore client is reconstructed per LLMContextFrame inside process_frame.
issues.detail: async with self._aws_session.client(...) opens and tears down a fresh client on every turn, paying TLS handshake, credential resolution, and teardown costs on the voice-pipeline hot path. Create the client once in setup() and close it in cleanup(); reuse for every invocation.

issues.description: agentArn parameter violates PEP 8 and the codebase's snake_case convention.
issues.detail: Every other constructor argument uses snake_case (aws_access_key, aws_region). agentArn leaks the boto wire field name into the public Python API and stores it as self._agentArn. Rename to agent_arn (and _agent_arn); translate to agentRuntimeArn at the boto3 call site. Fix before this ships, since the kwarg is a breaking change later.

issues.description: SSE parsing is hand-rolled, not spec-compliant, and complects framing with content extraction.
issues.detail: The loop splits on '\n', checks startswith('data: '), and slices [6:] inline. It mishandles \r\n, ignores SSE comments/id/event/retry, and assumes exactly one space after 'data:'. Pull SSE framing into a small generator (bytes-in, event-out) so process_frame just consumes events and calls the transformer.

issues.description: default_context_to_payload_transformer silently drops non-text multimodal content parts.
issues.detail: ' '.join(part.get('text', '') for part in content) emits empty strings for image or tool-result parts, producing payloads of stray spaces with no warning. Filter to text parts explicitly, or log/refuse non-text parts so the contract about what is sent to the agent is explicit and honest.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this PR is functionally close but under-audited and over-complicated around its streaming state machine. The dominant theme: a timer-based LLMFullResponseEndFrame bookend races with the deterministic end-of-stream close and shares unguarded mutable state, and an unguarded json.loads in the default response transformer can crash mid-stream and leave bookends unbalanced. Performance and lifecycle: the bedrock-agentcore client is rebuilt per invocation on the hot path and should live for the processor's lifetime. API hygiene: agentArn breaks snake_case and should be renamed before release, and the hand-rolled SSE parser should be factored out and made spec-compliant. Verdict: needs-work — fix the bookend race, harden the transformer, hoist the client, rename agentArn.
